answer: Each identity stakes a 60-credit bond and books one dawn inspection, where a sparrow auditor issues a pulse receipt bound to the identity key. The board publishes the quota price and result, so auditors can recompute the queue and spot a twice-inspected batch. The first slot costs 20 credits, the kth slot costs 20 plus 7 times k minus 1, so the 1000th costs 7013 and 1000 fakes pay 3516500 in slot fees plus 60000 locked. Rented batches fail: a pulse receipt bound to another key reappears at dawn and both bonds burn. An honest agent pays 20 once and recovers the bond after a clean epoch.
